trust_decision.summary: ReadWriteLock trusts the on-disk lock database's schema: the first statement of every acquire makes SQLite load the whole schema with no step or length bound, and the busy timeout does not cover that load; the fix bounds it in _configure_and_begin via a progress-handler step budget and SQLITE_LIMIT_LENGTH.

landing_point.why: _configure_and_begin runs the first SQL statements (PRAGMA journal_mode, BEGIN, SELECT sqlite_master) of every acquire; the summary 'every acquire stalls regardless of timeout' leads straight to it and to _execute_waiting.

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: Async wrapper reaches the same _configure_and_begin through src/filelock/_async_read_write.py:225-240 -> src/filelock/_read_write.py:655-666 and needed no change

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No route is left to dismiss: every acquire funnels into one function, so the only arguable omission would be the constructor's validation connect (src/filelock/_read_write.py:529-531), which runs no statement and so loads no schema.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A contended acquire must still wait in SQLite's busy handler up to its timeout and raise Timeout (and stay cancellable by sliced busy waits); a fresh empty lock file and a normal lock database must still lock. A wall-clock bound or a step budget that also counts the busy wait would turn legitimate contention into ValueError; refusing any non-empty database breaks existing lock files.

O6_input_shapes: schema b-tree with deep interior pages fanning out to ~661**4 rows in a 5-page file (step budget)
single schema row whose SQL text spans a self-referencing overflow chain, ~1 MB in a sparse file (SQLITE_LIMIT_LENGTH)
both read mode (BEGIN + SELECT sqlite_master) and write mode (BEGIN EXCLUSIVE)

O7_producer.where: The schema is file content loaded lazily by SQLite on the first statement in src/filelock/_read_write.py:965-967; no project-side producer.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a constructor-time validation statement (e.g. a header/format or journal_mode probe) on the validation connection, outside _configure_and_begin
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The constructor already opens a validation connection to reject bad files (WAL check); a maintainer could naturally add a SQL probe there, which loads the schema before any bound is set.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a status/holds probe that runs a statement on a fresh connection to ask whether the database is locked
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Lock libraries commonly expose is_locked-style queries; one implemented via a short SQLite statement would reach the same schema load on a different path from acquire.

O9_family: resource exhaustion: unbounded SQLite schema load from an attacker-supplied database file (CWE-400)

O10_build.toolchain: Python >=3.11, hatchling build, pytest (+pytest-timeout); stdlib sqlite3
O10_build.project_tests: tests/test_read_write.py, tests/test_read_write_unit.py (no schema-bound tests at pinned commit; fix adds them at fix.diff:1577-1629)

j.j_sites_touched: src/filelock/_read_write.py (DoS part); _windows.py and _api.py changes belong to the bundled link/ACL fix
j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Refuse lock files above a byte size or page count before connecting, which misses the 5-page deep b-tree shape, or wrap the statements in a wall-clock deadline that also fires on legitimate contention.

out_of_scope_notes: Fix commit 5e3f2ec bundles a separate link-following/journal-planting fix (private hard link directory, Windows ACL checks, _remove_link_directory) in src/filelock/_read_write.py and src/filelock/_windows.py; that is the c_same_check_name signal, not this DoS.
Hot-journal replay size beside the database is pager work a VM step budget would not bound; addressed upstream by the private-link change, not by _bounded_schema.
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell); tiny_repo flag inferred from ~22 source files under src/filelock.
